text.content: CWAM B5 VOM R8 high-utilization B192 probe

Determine whether increasing the no-checkpointing micro-batch from 128 to 192 per rank converts remaining B200 memory headroom into higher sustained sample throughput while preserving finite training and aligned-memory intervention dependence.

Complete 100 finite optimizer steps on 8 B200s; no OOM, traceback, NCCL, or nonfinite gradients; peak memory below 90%; final matched validation aligned action loss at least 1% below both exact-zero and shuffled memory. Select B192 for formal 20k only if samples/s materially exceeds B128; otherwise select B128.
88f3c95c18a3f3195b66e35b2cd8f6ecfe595b81 training source; 1fe84a6 parameterized R8 probe launcher (pushed)

R4 step-500 model-only warm start; optimizer/scheduler/trainer restart at zero; R6-A dynamic-exclusive full final-delta architecture; R7 policy ranking weight=1.0, relative margin=1%, warmup=50; 100 steps; batch 192/rank, DP8, global 1536; token cap 444000; activation checkpointing none; validation at steps 0 and 100; checkpoint at 100.

RoboCasa365 B4 processed split plus 1,143,698-record triple-view Wan latent cache and episode-safe t-36/t-24/t-12 visual-history sidecar; same stream and data contract as B128 and R7; no future lookup.
pyrogpucompute1; 8 x NVIDIA B200 183359 MiB; batch 192/rank; effective global batch 1536.

Steady-state seconds/step and samples/s versus B128; GPU utilization, peak memory, and power; finite/nonzero action gradients; aligned/zero/shuffle action losses and relative gains; checkpoint completeness.

This is the final bounded utilization probe before the 20k formal launch. It is isolated from B128, starts from the same R4 model-only checkpoint, and uses fresh optimizer/scheduler/trainer state. B192 is selected only if it improves useful sample throughput, not merely memory occupancy.
